newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Mugabe says G-15 future lies in success in trade.
newsitem.headline: Mugabe says G-15 future lies in success in trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe said on Sunday the future of the developing countries' Group of 15 (G-15), set up to spearhead trade between the world's poorest continents, hinged on deeds rather than words.

He told a three-day trade promotion summit of the G-15 in Harare that the organisation was now less enthusiastic about boosting trade between Africa, Asia and Latin America than in the early days of its existence. But he gave no figures.
"The continued existence of the G-15 hinges, to a large extent, on our ability to translate words into action," Mugabe said at the summit.
"The implementation of various projects seems to have lost momentum, and the enthusiasm that accompanied their launch is gradually dissipating," he said.
The G-15 was set up in 1989 along the lines of the Group of Seven industrialised countries, but has been widely in the past as a mere talkshop.
On Sunday, Mugabe said: "It certainly is the collective hope of all of us that this meeting will emerge with concrete guidelines on increasing South-South trade".
A G-15 report says out of 21 projects initiated since its formation, only four have been concluded, four others were at an advanced stage of implementation and nine still on paper.

The G-15 has retained its original name though it now comprises 16 countries, namely Algeria, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Jamaica, Malaysia, Mexico, Nigeria, Senegal, Peru, Venezuela, Yugoslavia and Zimbabwe.
